caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1186 of 2004
lawyer:
A.K.M. Shahidul Huq, Advocate-on Record ------ For the petitioners 
Respondents ------ Not represented.
parties:
1. Padma Bibi being dead, her heirs: 1(Ka), Mohammad Rashid & others ------ Petitioners.
Vs.
The Headmaster & Secretary, Moheshkhali High School & others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
2. Padma Bibi, the predecessor of the petitioner Nos. 1(Ka) to 1 (Gha) and Dhalu Bibi, the predecessor of the petitioner Nos. 2 to 4, filed Other Suit No. 229 of 1981 in the Court of the learned Munsif (now Assistant Judge), Sadar, Cox's Bazar, praying for declaration of title, confirmation of possession and also permanent injunction in respect of the suit land contending, inter alia, that the suit land originally belonged to Monsur Ali, father of the plaintiffs who was raiyat under Khirode Chandia Roy, the superior landlord; Monsur Ali while owning and possessing the suit land got his daughters Padma Bibi and Dhalu Bibi married with their husbands who were domesticated and Monsur Ali constructed dwelling houses in the suit land for their dwelling; after the death of Monsur Ali, Padma Bibi and Dhalu Bibi as well as proforma defendant No.4, their cousin, became owners of the suit land but Padma Bibi and Mats Bibi, being poor, the proforma defendant No.4 did not claim any portion in the suit land and lived elsewhere, Padma Bibi and Dhalu Bibi being pardanashin as well as illiterate, during M.R.R. operation, the defendant No.1 taking that advantage created M.R.R. Khatian in the name of Maheskhali High School and subsequently the defendant No.1 threatened to dispossess the plaintiffs from the suit land hence the suit. The defendant No.1 contested the suit and filed written statement, contending inter alia that after the death of Khirode Chandra Roy, Ajit Kumar Roy became the landlord and Mansur Ali having abandoned the suit land Ajit Kumar Roy took khan possession thereof and thereafter gifted the suit land along with other lands in favour of Moheshkhali High school; the Managing Committee of the school dismissed Mostaque Ahmed ; Chowdhury, the Assistant Headmaster of the said school and then he out of grudge inducted the plaintiffs in the suit land who then constructed two houses in the suit land and while the defendant No.1 took initiative to evict the plaintiffs from the suit land they filed the instant suit. After transfer of this suit to the Court of Assistant Judge, Ramoo Upazilla, Cox's Bazar the above suit was renumbered as ; Other Suit No. 14 of 1986. The trial Court after hearing dismissed the suit. The plaintiff than preferred Other Appeal No. 148 of 1986 and the learned Additional District Judge, Cox's Bazar, after hearing, allowed the appeal; The defendant No.1 then moved the High Court Division and obtained Rule in Civil Revision No. 2100 of 1996 and after hearing the High Court Division made the Rule absolute. 

 3. The learned counsel for the plaintiff/petitioners submits that the High Court Division, committed error in not considering that admittedly Monsur Ali, the predecessor of the plaintiffs, being a raiyat under Khirode Chandra Roy, the superior landlord, owned and possessed the suit land and after his death, the plaintiffs have been owning and possessing the suit land by constructing dwelling houses thereon and that there is no materials on record to show that during the lifetime of Mansur Ali his possession in the suit was disturbed by the landlord; that by way of continued possession over the statutory period he plaintiffs acquired right title and interest in the suit land; in Ext.2, the Local Inspection Report submitted by the learned Advocate Commissioner who ho conducted the inspection stated that নালিশী জমিতে বসতগৃহস্থিত আছে। নালিশী জমিতে ৫ খানা ঘর আছে। যথা একটি রিকসা ও টেকসী রাখার ঘর, একটি ছাগল রাখার ঘর ও একটি গোয়ালঘর দেখিতে পাইয়াছেন। তিনি তাহার প্রতিবেদনে আরও উল্লেখ করিয়াছেন যে, বসত ৪ গৃহের মধ্যে মূল বড় গৃহটির বয়স ৬০/৬৫ বৎসর এবং বাকী গৃহ পরে নির্মিত হইয়াছেন and D.W.1 in his cross-examination also admitted that বর্তমান বাদিনীগন বসতগৃহ নির্মানে এবং ফলবাস বৃক্ষাদি রোপনে নালিশী জমিতে দখলকার আছেন and the High Court Division approached the whole case on a wrong way by placing much reliance upon Ext. Ka, the deed of gift alleged to have been executed by Ajit Kumar Roy, without at all considering that the said gift was not acted upon. The learned counsel further submits that the High Court Division from the evidence on record further found that in support of the suit the plaintiffs only produced Exhibit, the A.S. Khatian, and no other document was filed to substantiate the case of the plaintiff and in the above R.S. Khatian the name of Khirode Chandra Roy was shown as the superior landlord but under him the name of Mansur Ali, the father of original plaintiffs, was also shown as raiyat and dag numbers 1682 and 1684 are described homestead and khilla and on the other hand the defendant produced as many as 19 exhibits in Ka and Kha series and Exhibit Ka is the deed of gift given by Ajit Kumar Roy in the year 1944 in favour of Moheskhali High School and it includes the suit land and Exhibit Kha (4) is the Duplicate Carbon Receipt, Exhibit Kha(5) to Kha (13) are rent receipts showing payment of rent in the name of the above school and that the trial court, on consideration of Exhibits Ka and Kha series duly found that the suit land was gifted to the above school by Ajit Kumar Roy and the suit land belongs to the school. 

 4. As it appears in the plaint the defendant No.1 was described as Headmaster and  Secretary of Moheskhali High School, the defendant No.2 was described as Circle Officer Development, Moheskhali, the defendant No.3 was described as Officer-in-charge Moheskhali Police Station and defendant No.4 was merely a proforma defendant No. 4 and the High Court Division considering that the plaintiff filed the suit on 18.3.81 for declaration of their title in the suit land, confirmation of their possession and also for permanent injunction restraining the defendant Nos. 1, 2 and 3 from disturbing the peaceful possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land and that in the plaint the defendant No.1 has been described as Headmaster and Secretary of Moheskhali High School, held that there is no basis for instituting the suit against Headmaster or Secretary of Moheskhali High School excluding the school itself and how the decree as passed by the appellate Court could be executed specially when the suit land does not belong to the Secretary or Headmaster of the above school and further how the defendant No.1 not being owner of the suit land could be restrained from disturbing the possession of the plaintiffs in the suit land and so the suit having been filed against a wrong person is not maintainable. The High Court Division further held that the settled principle of law is that the plaintiff is to prove his/her own case but in support of plaint case the plaintiffs, except R.S. Khatian, did not produce any other document or any rent receipt and that plaintiff No.1, who deposed as P.W. 1, stated that নালিশী তপসিলের জমি মহেশখালী থানার অন্তর্গত বদদ মহেশখালী মৌজার জমিদার ক্ষিরোদ চন্দ্র রায়ের অধীনস্থ ১/২ নং বাদীনির পিতা মোনছুর আলীর রায়তী স্বত্বীয় খাস দখলী জমি ছিল। তৎমতে আর, এস, ১০৮ নং খতিয়ান চূড়ান্ত রহিয়াছে but this R.S. Khatian was prepared as back as in the year 1932 and the plaintiffs did not produce any other document to prove that they are still maintaining possession of the suit land and in cross examination P.W. 1 admitted that মোনছুর আমাদের পিতা তৎমর্মে আমরা কাগজ পত্র দাখিল করি নাই।
